result.title: What Moves a LoCoMo Score? Memory Context, Answer Prompts and Judges
result.comment: 13 pages, 2 figures. Answers, judge verdicts, human-check grades and scoring script: https://github.com/becos-ai/locomo-results
result.summary: LoCoMo is a widely reported benchmark for long-term conversational memory, but published scores mix memory quality with choices of answer prompt, judge and baseline layout that are rarely reported together. We measure how much these choices move a score, and evaluate Becos, a team memory system for coding agents, as a black box under all of them: ten conversations (1,540 questions), two answer models (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini), two answer prompts and three LLM judges, against a whole-conversation baseline rerun under identical conditions. Changing only the judge moves a score by up to 7.2 points and changing only the answer prompt by up to 9.3. A blind human check of 150 answers finds the judges reliable when they agree, and the primary judge's errors on disputed answers working against Becos rather than for it. Becos answers from a context with 90% fewer characters than the whole conversation. Its configuration was developed on LoCoMo itself, so there is no held-out set. With gpt-4o-mini answers it scores clearly higher than the whole conversation (79.7 vs 73.0 with the short prompt, paired 95% interval for the difference +3.8 to +9.5; 88.8 vs 77.5 with a step-by-step prompt). With gpt-4.1-mini answers the two score about the same (83.2 vs 83.1; 92.5 vs 92.1). We release every answer and verdict and the scoring script.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在 LoCoMo 长程对话记忆基准上，分别量化答案提示、评判模型和基线设置对分数的单独影响，并把 Becos 记忆系统作为黑盒在该基准上评测，公开全部答案、判分与评分脚本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是文本记忆任务的评测敏感性分析（仅换评判者可移动最高 7.2 分、仅换提示可移动 9.3 分），且系统只依据约少 90% 字符的上下文作答，可能为 LVR 中证据筛选、上下文压缩与 latent 推理评价的判分稳健性提供可供核查的线索。
